key_insight: The study shows that LLMs can generate varied colonoscopy-prep conversations, but response correctness and safety still vary enough to require careful oversight.
clinical_relevance: Interactive AI assistants may help patients understand prep instructions and ask questions, potentially improving bowel-prep adherence before colonoscopy.
method: Generated 250 synthetic patient–AI coach dialogues per model across 5 leading LLMs.
Used 3–7 question-answer pairs on diet, medications, and other prep topics.
Had medical experts and automated judges rate question difficulty, response correctness, error type, diversity, and harmfulness.
evidence_signal: Five LLMs were compared using human expert review, LLM-as-a-judge evaluation, diversity metrics (Distinct-1/2, entropy), and permutation tests at the dialogue level.
watch_item: Synthetic dialogue performance may not translate directly to real patients, and incorrect advice must be reliably filtered before any clinical use.
paper_title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Colonoscopy Preparation Assistance: Correctness and Diversity in Synthetic Dialogues
